questions.question: Which description fits the **RequestGroup** resource?
options: A group of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one".

Describes the intention of how one or more practitioners intend to deliver care for a particular patient, group or community for a period of time, possibly limited to care for a specific condition or set of conditions.
This resource includes all the people and organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care for a patient.
A request to supply a diet, formula feeding (enteral) or oral nutritional supplement to a patient/resident.
questions.explanation: **RequestGroup**: A group of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one". The other descriptions belong to **CarePlan**, **CareTeam**, **NutritionOrder**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “A group of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one".”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **RequestGroup** (Clinical › Care Provision).

questions.question: Where does **RequestGroup** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **RequestGroup** is in **Clinical › Care Provision**: Planning and ordering care: care plans, care teams and goals, orders for tests, procedures or referrals (ServiceRequest), diet orders, eyewear prescriptions and risk assessments.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **RequestGroup** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of RequestGroup are `status` (1..1), `intent` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **RequestGroup** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of RequestGroup: `status`, `intent`. `status`: draft | active | on-hold | revoked | completed | entered-in-error | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
